subject: maths
title: Maps and Locations: Compass Points, Directions and Grid References
seo_title: Year 3 Maps and Locations Worksheets: Compass Directions and Grid Maps (Free)
standard_text: Interpret and create two dimensional representations of familiar environments, locating key landmarks and objects relative to each other
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on maps and locations: read a school map, use north, south, east and west, follow directions on a grid map, bird’s-eye views and grid references like B3. 100 questions with an answer key, Australian Curriculum aligned and great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: North is at the top of most maps. Going clockwise: north, east, south, west.
key_sub: When you follow directions, count the squares you move, not the square you start on. A grid reference gives the letter (across) first, then the number.
body_html:
What a map is

A map or plan shows a place from above, like a bird flying over it. This is called a bird’s-eye view. Each shape on the map stands for a real place.

Where is it?

Use position words: next to, between, left of, right of. Maps also use the compass points. North is usually at the top. Going clockwise: north, east, south, west. Remember it with “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix”.

On the mapCompass point
upnorth
downsouth
righteast
leftwest
Example

What is the first place you reach going straight south from the library?

South is down the map. From the library, go down: C2 is empty, C3 is the garden.

Answer: the garden

Follow directions on a grid

Count the squares you move. Do not count the square you start on. Do one direction at a time.

Grid references

Many maps have letters across the top and numbers down the side. A grid reference like B4 names one square. Go across to the letter first, then down to the number.

Example

On the classroom plan, what is in square E2?

Go across to column E, then down to row 2.

Answer: the sink

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up east and westNorth at the top, then go clockwise: Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix. East is on the right.
Using left and right of the page for a person who faces southTurn the map so you face the same way as the person
Counting the starting squareCount the moves, not the square you stand on
Reading a grid reference number first (B3 as C2)Letter first, across; then the number
Choosing the side view when asked for a bird’s-eye viewImagine looking straight down from above

faq.q: What do Year 3 students learn about maps in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 3 (AC9M3SP02) students read and draw simple maps and plans of familiar places, such as the classroom, school or park, and describe where landmarks are using words like next to, between, left, right and the compass points.

faq.q: How can my child remember north, east, south and west?
faq.a: Start at north at the top and go clockwise, saying “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix”. East is on the right of a map and west is on the left.

faq.q: How do you read a grid reference like B3?
faq.a: Go across to column B first, then down to row 3. The letter always comes first.

faq.q: Are maps and directions in the NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: Yes. Space questions in NAPLAN numeracy often ask students to read a simple map, follow directions or find a location. Practising with grid maps like these helps.

sets.title: Read a school map: next to, between and closest

items.q: Which of these places is closest to the gate?
items.e: The sandpit is right next to the gate. The others are further away.

items.q: What is in the bottom left corner of the map?
items.e: Bottom means the bottom row. Left means the left side. The playground is in the bottom left corner.

items.q: What is between the canteen and the art room?
items.e: Find the canteen and the art room. They are in the same column. The place in the middle of them is the toilets.

items.q: What is between the hall and the office?
items.e: Find the hall and the office. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the library.

items.q: What is just to the right of the library on the map?
items.e: Look one square to the right of the library. It is the office. The hall is on its left.

items.q: Which place is next to the bike racks?
items.e: Next to means touching, side by side. The classrooms are just above the bike racks. The gate is 2 squares away.

items.q: Which place covers the most squares on the map?
items.e: The oval covers 4 squares. The hall, the car park and the classrooms cover 2 squares each.

items.q: What is between the toilets and the playground?
items.e: Find the toilets and the playground. They are in the same column. The place in the middle of them is the art room.

items.q: The canteen is next to two places. What are they?
c: the toilets and the art room
items.e: Look at the squares touching the canteen: the hall is just above it and the toilets are just below it. The square on its right is empty.

items.q: How many squares is it from the canteen straight down to the playground?
items.e: From the canteen go down: toilets (1), art room (2), playground (3). Do not count the canteen.

items.q: How many squares do you walk from the gate, straight up the map, to the office? (Do not count the gate.)
items.e: From the gate (D5) go up: D4 is 1, D3 is 2, D2 is 3 and the office (D1) is 4. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Which of these is not on the map?
items.e: Read every label on the map. There is a canteen, a library and bike racks, but no swimming pool.

items.q: What is in the top right corner of the map?
items.e: Top means the top row. Right means the right side. The car park is in the top right corner. The hall is in the top left.

items.q: What is just to the left of the sandpit on the map?
items.e: Look one square to the left of the sandpit. It is part of the playground. The gate is on its right.

items.q: What is between the playground and the gate?
items.e: Find the playground and the gate. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the sandpit.

items.q: Which place is next to the oval?
items.e: The car park touches the top of the oval. The garden and the office do not touch it: there is a gap.

items.q: How many squares does the oval cover on the map?
items.e: The oval is 2 squares across and 2 squares down: 2 rows of 2 squares. 2 + 2 = 4 squares.

items.q: What is just above the art room on the map?
items.e: Look up from the art room, one square. That square is the toilets. The playground is just below it.

items.q: What is between the library and the car park?
items.e: Find the library and the car park. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the office.

items.q: Which is closer to the office?
items.e: Count squares from the office. The garden is 3 squares away. The art room is 6 squares away.

sets.title: Position words and compass directions: north, south, east, west

items.q: On most maps, which way is north?
c: towards the left of the map
towards the top of the map
towards the right of the map
towards the bottom of the map
items.e: Maps usually have north at the top. The compass on the map shows N pointing up.

items.q: Aarav stands at the gate and faces north. Where is the sandpit for him?
items.e: Aarav faces north, the same way as the top of the map. So his left is west and his right is east. The sandpit is west of him, so it is on his left.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight west from the office?
items.e: West is to the left on the map. Go west from the office, square by square. The first place you reach is the library. Going east would give the car park.

items.q: The art room is ___ of the canteen.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The art room is south of the canteen.

items.q: The hall is ___ of the office.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The hall is west of the office. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north from the garden?
items.e: North is up on the map. Go north from the garden, square by square. The first place you reach is the library. Going south would give the sandpit.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight west from the garden?
items.e: West is to the left on the map. Go west from the garden, square by square. The first place you reach is the toilets. Going east would give the oval.

items.q: William stands at the library and faces south. Where is the hall for him?
items.e: William faces south, towards the bottom of the map, so his left and right are swapped compared with the page. Turn the map upside down to check. His left is east. The hall is west, so it is on his right.

items.q: The library is ___ of the hall.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The library is east of the hall. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: Liam walks east to the canteen. Which way does he walk to come straight back?
items.e: To come back you go the opposite way. East and west are opposites. North and south are opposites.

items.q: The bike racks are ___ of the classrooms.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The bike racks are south of the classrooms.

items.q: Harper stands in the garden and faces north. Where is the library for her?
items.e: Harper faces north, the same way as the top of the map. So her left is west and her right is east. The library is north of her, so it is in front of her.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight south from the library?
items.e: South is down on the map. Go south from the library, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: The canteen is ___ of the toilets.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The canteen is north of the toilets.

items.q: Grace stands in the garden and faces south. Where is the sandpit for her?
items.e: Grace faces south, towards the bottom of the map, so her left and right are swapped compared with the page. Turn the map upside down to check. Her left is east. The sandpit is south, so it is in front of her.

items.q: The oval is ___ of the garden.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The oval is east of the garden. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north from the sandpit?
items.e: North is up on the map. Go north from the sandpit, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: Ruby stands at the toilets and faces east. Where is the canteen for her?
items.e: Ruby faces east. Her left is north and her right is south. The canteen is north, so it is on her left.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight east from the toilets?
items.e: East is to the right on the map. Go east from the toilets, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: On a map with north at the top, which direction is to the right?
items.e: Going clockwise from north: north (up), east (right), south (down), west (left). Many students mix up east and west.

sets.title: Follow directions on a grid map

items.q: Which directions take you from the gate to the gum tree?
items.e: The gate is in A5 and the gum tree is in C3. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on: 2 squares east, then 2 squares north.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares north, then 2 squares east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 2 squares north to A3, then 2 squares east to C3. The gum tree is in C3.

items.q: Lachlan starts at the red dot. He goes 2 squares east. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at C4. Go 2 squares east to E4. That is square D. If you mix up east and west you land on A.

items.q: Start at the kiosk. Go 2 squares west, then 1 square south. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F1. Go 2 squares west to D1, then 1 square south to D2. The bench is in D2.

items.q: Matilda starts at the red dot. She goes 1 square north, then 3 squares west. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 1 square north to F4, then 3 squares west to C4. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Which directions take you from the slide to the shelter?
items.e: The slide is in E1 and the shelter is in D4. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on: 1 square west, then 3 squares south.

items.q: Start at the BBQ. Go 3 squares east, then 1 square north. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 3 squares east to D3, then 1 square north to D2. The bench is in D2.

items.q: Start at the rotunda. Go 3 squares north, then 1 square east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at C5. Go 3 squares north to C2, then 1 square east to D2. The bench is in D2.

items.q: Isla starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares south. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at C1. Go 3 squares south to C4. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Kai starts at the red dot. He goes 2 squares south, then 3 squares east. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at B1. Go 2 squares south to B3, then 3 squares east to E3. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Which directions take you from the pond to the bin?
items.e: The pond is in B2 and the bin is in E3. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on: 3 squares east, then 1 square south.

items.q: Ethan starts at the red dot. He goes 2 squares west, then 3 squares north. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at E4. Go 2 squares west to C4, then 3 squares north to C1. That is square B. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: How many squares east is it from the BBQ to the bin?
items.e: Count the moves: the BBQ is in A3 and the bin is in E3. That is 4 squares east. Do not count the BBQ square.

items.q: Sienna walks from the swings straight to the slide. Which direction does she walk?
items.e: The slide (E1) is to the right of the swings (C1) in the same row. Right on the map is east.

items.q: Mei starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares north. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares north to E2. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: How many squares north is it from the flag to the kiosk?
items.e: The flag is in F4 and the kiosk is in F1. Count the moves up: 3 squares north.

items.q: Jack starts at the red dot. He goes 3 squares west. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at E2. Go 3 squares west to B2. That is square B. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Oliver starts at the toilets. He goes 3 squares south, 2 squares east, then 1 square south. Where is he?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 3 squares south to A4, then 2 squares east to C4, then 1 square south to C5. The rotunda is there.

items.q: Start at the tap. Go 2 squares south, then 2 squares west. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F2. Go 2 squares south to F4, then 2 squares west to D4. The shelter is in D4.

items.q: Chloe starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares east, then 2 squares north. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 3 squares east to D5, then 2 squares north to D3. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

sets.title: Bird’s-eye views and grid references like B3

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bins?
items.e: Go across first to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bins are in column E, row 3: E3. Always write the letter first.

items.q: The reading mat covers two squares. What are they?
items.e: The reading mat is in row 3, in columns C and D. So it covers C3 and D3.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the laptops?
items.e: Go across first to find the letter, then down to find the number. The laptops are in column A, row 4: A4. Always write the letter first.

items.q: What is in square E4?
items.e: Find column E along the top, then go down to row 4. Square E4 is the lockers.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the door?
items.e: Go across first to find the letter, then down to find the number. The door is in column C, row 4: C4. Always write the letter first.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: A round top with 4 small circles around it: a round table with 4 stools, seen from above.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: You can see a pillow at one end and a blanket. It is a bed seen from above.

items.q: A drink can stands on a table. What shape does its top look like in a bird’s-eye view?
items.e: From above you see only the round top of the can: a circle. From the side the can looks like a rectangle.

items.q: What is in square D1?
items.e: Find column D along the top, then go down to row 1. Square D1 is the window. Mixing up the letter and the number (column A, row 4) gives the laptops.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: You can see the windscreen, the roof and the 4 wheels poking out. It is a car seen from above.

items.q: What is in square B2?
items.e: Find column B along the top, then go down to row 2. Square B2 is the teacher’s desk.

items.q: The whiteboard covers two squares. What are they?
items.e: The whiteboard is in row 1, in columns A and B. So it covers A1 and B1.

items.q: Which picture shows the table with 4 chairs from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture D shows the table with 4 chairs from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: Which picture shows the car from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture B shows the car from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: Which square is empty?
items.e: Look at row 4: A4 is the laptops, C4 is the door and E4 is the lockers. B4 has nothing in it.

items.q: Which picture shows the tree from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture C shows the tree from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: Which picture shows the house from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture B shows the house from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the sink?
items.e: Go across first to find the letter, then down to find the number. The sink is in column E, row 2: E2. Always write the letter first.

items.q: What is in square C3?
items.e: Find column C along the top, then go down to row 3. Square C3 is the reading mat.

items.q: Which picture shows the cup of hot chocolate from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture A shows the cup of hot chocolate from above. Picture B shows it from the side.

sets.title: Choose the right map and solve real-life problems

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. The tigers are ___ of the reptiles.
items.e: The tigers are just above the reptiles. Up on the map is north.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. The seals are ___ of the penguins.
items.e: The seals are just to the right of the penguins. Right on the map is east.

items.q: Which map shows the pond east of the tree and the bench south of the tree?
items.e: East is to the right and south is down. The pond must be just right of the tree and the bench just below it. Mixing up east and west puts the pond on the left. That is map A.

items.q: Ava’s house is south of the school. Which way does she walk to get from school to home?
items.e: The house is south of the school, so she walks south. North would take her further away.

items.q: What does the key (legend) on a map tell you?
c: what the symbols on the map mean
items.e: A key lists the symbols used on the map and what each one means, for example a blue shape for water. The compass shows north.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. The playground covers two squares. What are their grid references?
items.e: The playground is in row 4, in columns D and E. Letter first: D4 and E4.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. Which directions take the class from the entrance to the penguins?
items.e: The entrance is C5 and the penguins are E3. Go 2 squares east (C to E) and 2 squares north (row 5 to row 3). Going west would take you to the reptiles.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. Which animals are between the lions and the reptiles?
items.e: The lions, tigers and reptiles are in column A. The tigers are in the middle.

items.q: Noah faces south. The canteen is on his left. Which direction is the canteen from him?
items.e: When you face south, your left hand points east. Try it: face the bottom of the map and hold out your left arm. On the page left is west, but Noah is facing the other way.

items.q: Matilda writes a grid reference on a street map. Which is written the right way?
items.e: Write the letter (across) first, then the number (down or up). D4 is right; 4D has them the wrong way round.

items.q: Which map shows the bin between the bench and the tree?
items.e: Between means in the middle of the other two, in a straight line. Only one map has the bin in the middle, with the bench on one side and the tree on the other. That is map C.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. The class eats lunch in the picnic area. Which animals are between the kangaroos and the picnic area?
items.e: Row 1 has the lions, the kangaroos, the emus and the picnic area. The emus are in the middle of the kangaroos and the picnic area.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. What is in square E2?
items.e: Find column E along the top, then go down to row 2. Square E2 is the café.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. Each square on the map is 20 metres. How far is it from the entrance straight north to the koalas?
items.e: From the entrance (C5) to the koalas (C3) is 2 squares. 2 × 20 = 40 metres. Counting the entrance square too gives 3 squares, or 60 metres.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. Kai leaves the toilets and goes 4 squares north, then 3 squares east. Which animals does he reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 4 squares north to A1, then 3 squares east to D1. The emus are in D1. Do not count the toilets square as one of the 4.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. From the entrance, the class walks 2 squares north. Which animals do they see?
items.e: Start at C5. Go 2 squares north to C3. The koalas are in C3. Counting the entrance square as 1 would stop you 1 square short.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. Amelia stands at the entrance and faces north. Where is the gift shop for her?
items.e: Facing north is facing the top of the map, so her right is east. The gift shop (E5) is east of the entrance (C5).

items.q: Which map shows the flag north of the tent?
items.e: North is towards the top, where the arrow points. The flag must be just above the tent. The flag below the tent would be south of it. That is map D.

items.q: The class is on a school excursion to the zoo. What is the grid reference of the penguins?
items.e: The penguins are in column E and row 3. Write the letter first: E3.

items.q: Ruby draws a plan of her bedroom. The desk is west of the bed and the door is south of the desk. Which plan is right? (The bed is blue and the desk is brown.)
items.e: West is to the left and south is down. The desk is just left of the bed and the door is just below the desk. That is map B.
